evidence: Two rules decide whether a bond window cuts a coordination shell, both kept unchanged by candidate 6 and both now readings of the shell module (src/llm/context/shells.js): the Workbench asks on the CN margin (cnMarginCut: the window overlaps the shell and holds fewer partner atoms by >= max(0.5, 15 % of the shell's CN)), compute_bond_angles refuses on the coordination counts (countsCut: more than half the central atoms unbonded, or fewer than 60 % with the most common count). On 149 natural windows (each closed shell's triplet around the polyhedron's centre in its whole shell, its first peak alone, its top 0.2 A earlier and later, and the Demo's historical Ta-Se windows) they agree on 134 (6 cut by both, 128 by neither). The counts alone refuse 11: dev-offcentre's whole Nb-Nb shell (3.40-4.24 A, CN 5.46, 52 % share the modal 5: its counts spread because the shell runs into the next) and 10 windows with the top 0.2 A early whose CN stays within the margin (the Demo's Ga-Ga 6.88-7.53 A, 11.2 of 11.9 at 52 %; dev-jahn-teller's Cu-K 6.87 of 8 at 38 %; ...). The CN margin alone asks on 4 first peaks whose counts form a sub-shell: the Demo's Ta-Se (3.25 of 6, 72 % have 3), dev-jahn-teller's four short Cu-F (3.98 of 6, 92 % have 4), the Demo's Se-Se (2.78 of 12, 76 %), dev-offcentre's one short Nb-O (0.89 of 6, 72 %). Both cut the spot check's 2.3-2.7 A and the old first-peak window 2.33-2.71 A on the Demo, two first peaks and two early cuts on the dev cases. Approved by the user, 2026-10-19. The new rule on the same 149 windows (validation/run.js shell-cuts at c15c8dd; one rule, windowCut: the CN margin where a window meets a shell, the counts only where the run reads no shell to compare): compute_bond_angles refuses 10 and the Workbench asks on exactly those 10 (they disagree on none); against the counts rule 15 change verdict, as the two readings predicted: 11 are no longer refused (dev-offcentre's whole Nb-Nb shell; the top 0.2 A early on dev-offcentre's O-O, dev-jahn-teller's Cu-K and F-K, dev-thermal-null's Ti-Ti and O-Ti, dev-symmetry-lowering's K-K, dev-chirality-trap's Cu-Cu, dev-fit-unconverged's Mg-Mg and O-O and the Demo's Ga-Ga, each within 15 % of its shell's CN) and 4 are refused now (the first peaks of the Demo's Ta-Se and Se-Se, dev-jahn-teller's Cu-F and dev-offcentre's Nb-O); 6 are refused by both, 128 by neither. With the five judgment-subset dev cases added since, the dev and Demo windows number 227: 16 refused, the Workbench asking on the same 16, and 22 change verdict (16 no longer refused, 6 refused now); the judgment cases' windows are not written here. A window apart from the first shell (the module reads first shells only, so it cannot say whether such a window cuts a later one) is judged by its counts, as before: the Demo's Se-Ta-Se 3.5-4.5 A (a later shell, 43 % with the modal 4) and Se-Ga-Se 2.9-3.6 A (99 % with no bond) are refused. Arms A, A+ and D on the dev set before and after: none of the 45 records moves (A+ reads no bond-angle window), so validation/baseline/arm-a-dev.json is not re-recorded. What the model sees: every compute_bond_angles result adds the shell reading and the counts' shares (+197 characters on the Demo's whole Ta-Se shell; the refusal of the spot check's window +248, its text the CN shortfall by path); the tool's description and schema are unchanged.
proposed_fix: Implemented as recommended: compute_bond_angles refuses on the Workbench's own CN-margin reading, so one rule decides a cut: shells.js windowCut, the CN margin where the window meets a shell with a CN (fewer partner atoms than the whole shell by at least max(0.5, 15 % of its CN)), the coordination counts only where the run reads no shell to compare (no partials file, no closed shell for the pair, no density for a CN, or a window apart from the first shell), as before. The clarifier asks on it and the tool refuses on it for each of its shellWindows (A-B, and B-C with a window of its own) unless window_confirmed: a window the Workbench did not question is not refused, and a whole shell never is (dev-offcentre's Nb-Nb). The refusal names the CN shortfall by path (shell_ab.cn_in_window of shell_ab.cn, in shell_ab.window_A); every result adds that shell reading (shell_ab, shell_bc) and the counts' modal, modal_share and unbonded_share as information, with no count-spread note (on the dev windows a spread under a passing margin was a whole shell running into the next, or a window within 15 % of its shell's CN, never a partial polyhedron, and the shares are in the data to quote); facts.coordination.whole_shell is the window's CN within the margin of the shell's. buildCopilotTools takes the run's plotFiles and runSettings (copilotRun.js and useCopilotRun.js pass the props' own), so the tool reads the clarifier's catalogue. window()'s counts option is gone; countsCut, MODAL_COORDINATION_SHARE and UNBONDED_APEX_FRACTION stay in shells.js as the fallback only. The coordination-shells skill's 60 % and "most" sentences (SKILL.md lines 61, 78, 79) are skill-lint allow-list entries, bound to the CN margin's CN_CHANGE_REL, until the skill fact-sync PR: the skill text is the user's.
